text:
morgan: quick follow-up on the MHA layout convo. i prototyped a tiny kernel switch that treats QKV as separate contiguous tensors vs an interleaved qkv blob. results are...surprising.
ian: curious — what's the input shapes and hw?
morgan: batch=8, seq=512, heads=16, head_dim=64 on A100. two variants: (1) qkv packed [B,S,3,H,hd] contiguous in memory, (2) q, k, v separate [B,S,H,hd] contiguous each.
sara: TLDR? which is faster?
morgan: separate wins for compute-bound dot products (~8-12% p50 token throughput) but packed wins when we do fused qkv->attn kernel because it avoids 2 extra memcpy passes in our current path. so depends a lot on whether we fuse the softmax+matmul path.
devon: that jives with my experiments. important nuance: packed layout can enable a single load+shuffle for SIMD lanes if we pick interleaving that matches register layout. but that also makes transposes expensive when we want NHWC vs NCHW views.
ian: can you paste the code snippet that did the load pattern?
morgan: sure:
```
// pseudo kernel load for packed qkv (layout = B,S,3,H,hd)
float* base = inputs + base_offset;
for (int s=0; s<seq; ++s) {
  for (int h=0; h<heads; ++h) {
    // single contiguous load of q,k,v block per token/head
    load16(base + s*stride + h*head_stride, reg_qkv);
    split_qkv(reg_qkv, q_reg, k_reg, v_reg);
  }
}
```
devon: nit: that sample assumes head_dim aligns to vector width. if head_dim%vec!=0 you pay shuffle + scalar tail. padding helps but increases memory.
sara: Right — so we need a policy: prefer padded head_dim and packed layout only when head_dim % VECTOR_WIDTH == 0 and seq smallish? But many models have odd head dims (e.g., 57, 64 mix).
ian: Another angle: runtime could keep canonical layout (separate q/k/v) and implement a zero-copy view for packed blob when model was exported that way. That way kernels declare their view requirements and runtime decides whether to materialize or just alias.
morgan: i like the alias idea but beware of stride aliasing. GPUs don't like non-contiguous strides for tensor cores unless we use explicit ldmatrix-like loads. Need to expose a 'stride hint' in kernel descriptor: allowed_strides = {contiguous, head_stride_interleaved, channel_major}.
devon: +1 for kernel descriptor. Also add a cost function: move_cost(bytes), transpose_cost(bytes, pattern), kernel_efficiency(layout, shape). We can use small microbench values gathered by benchbot.
benchbot: perf snapshot: packed->fused_attn: 14500 tokens/s; separate->fused_attn: 13100 tokens/s; packed->nonfused: 9800 tokens/s; separate->nonfused: 10850 tokens/s; measured on A100 40GB. details: seq=512, heads=16, head_dim=64.
sara: perfect. that suggests we should pick per-model heuristics: if fused_attn available and packed layout, choose packed. Otherwise prefer separate for generality.
ian: operationally, how does this show up in model import? we can't force producers to export one layout. suggest: during model onboarding, run a short profiler that exercises a few typical shapes and records which kernel path is best. store that in model metadata.
\dmorgan: (typo) devon:*
// continuing
morgan: exactly. we can add to model manifest: "preferred_mha_layout": "packed"|"separate"|"auto" and "layout_bench": {"seq":512,...} as small arrays. runtime picks layout or inserts a layout converter.
devon: converters are cheap if we amortize across many requests (cache converted weights) but memory cost increases. for Dedicated customers paying for memory it's fine; for Hosted we should prefer on-the-fly conversion or fallback kernels.
sara: also security/compliance note: Private clusters may forbid persistent conversions (writing converted model to disk). tag that.
ian: API boundary question: should kernel authors accept arbitrary strides and let runtime pass strided views, or should we limit kernel interface to a small set of canonical layouts and force runtime to convert?
\dmorgan: my vote: small canonical set. fewer kernels, easier reasoning. but provide an advanced opt-in path for strided views for expert kernels.
devon: same. and add regression tests: for each kernel, run shape grid {seq:32,128,512,2048} x {head_dim:32,64,96,128} and record break-even points. store as CSV in artifacts.
sara: can someone draft a short RFC addendum listing: kernel descriptor fields (allowed_strides, preferred_layouts, fallback_costs), onboarding profiler steps, and conversion caching policy?
ian: I'll take a first pass. timeline: draft by EOD Friday?
morgan: thanks. i'll attach microbench scripts and add a small note about ldmatrix-friendly packing.
devon: i'll enumerate GPU-specific loading patterns we should optimize for (A100,V100,H100).
sara: awesome. :thumbsup:
